ESP32 and Actuation

Role of the ESP32

The ESP32 implements the low-level actuation layer. It directly controls the three yarn-selection servomotors and acquires the synchronization microswitch.

The firmware file is:

servo_switch_usb.ino

GPIO Assignment

Function ESP32 GPIO
Servo 1 signal GPIO13
Servo 2 signal GPIO14
Servo 3 signal GPIO27
Microswitch input GPIO25

Three-Servo Selection Logic

Only one servo channel is active for each pixel:

Command Servo 1 Servo 2 Servo 3
C1 UP DOWN DOWN
C2 DOWN UP DOWN
C3 DOWN DOWN UP
DOWN DOWN DOWN DOWN

Initial experimental calibration values are:

const int UP_1 = 140;
const int DOWN_1 = 60;

const int UP_2 = 140;
const int DOWN_2 = 60;

const int UP_3 = 140;
const int DOWN_3 = 60;

These angles must be calibrated after mounting the custom 3D-Printed Servo Arms.

Microswitch Synchronization

The three-terminal microswitch is connected using its normally open contact:

Microswitch terminal Connection
COM ESP32 GND
NO ESP32 GPIO25
NC Not connected

The firmware uses the internal pull-up resistor:

pinMode(pinMicroswitch, INPUT_PULLUP);

Therefore the input is HIGH at rest and becomes LOW when the switch is pressed. A 50 ms debounce filter prevents one physical press from generating multiple events.

USB Serial Protocol

The ESP32 is connected to the Raspberry Pi through a USB cable. The cable powers the ESP32 board and carries serial messages; the servomotors are supplied separately.

The communication speed is:

115200 baud

Messages Received by the ESP32

Message Effect
C1 Select colour channel 1
C2 Select colour channel 2
C3 Select colour channel 3
DOWN Release all three channels

Messages Sent by the ESP32

Message Meaning
READY Initialization completed
NEXT Valid microswitch press detected
OK:C1, OK:C2, OK:C3 Requested servo position applied
OK:DOWN All servos set to inactive position
ERR:... Invalid serial command received

Arduino Project Organization

Arduino compiles all .ino files located in one sketch directory. The active firmware must therefore be kept in its own folder:

servo/
└── servo_switch_usb/
    └── servo_switch_usb.ino

Do not keep a previous complete sketch in the same folder, otherwise duplicated definitions of setup(), loop() and servo objects will prevent compilation.
